facts.text: Soundview’s name first appeared in early 20th century when developers branded the waterfront district with views toward the Long Island Sound.
The neighborhood sits on the Clason Point peninsula, bounded by the Cross Bronx Expressway, White Plains Road, Lacombe Avenue, and the Bronx River.
Soundview Park, built on a former landfill, is the largest park in the South Bronx and has been fully renovated with new trails and a boat launch.
The Bronx River Houses Tenant Association in Soundview became a model for resident leadership, inspiring nearby community groups in the 1980s and 1990s.
In 1947, NYCHA built a temporary housing project of 947 apartments in 473 Quonset huts in Soundview, a unique postwar solution.
The Sotomayor Houses honor former resident Supreme Court Justice Sonia Sotomayor, who lived there for 13 years starting in 1957.
